```{r}
dist <- list()
dist_name <- c(
  "0"  = "none",
  "10" = "other",
  "20" = "cut",
  "30" = "road",
  "40" = "fire",
  "50" = "biotic"
)

dist.forecastparams <- list()

count <- 1
for (dclass in names(dist.priors)) {
  dist.name <- as.character(dist_name[dclass])
  nclust <- length(dist.priors[[dclass]]$means)
  
  for (i in 1:nclust) {
    dist.forecastparams[[count]] <- list()
    dist.forecastparams[[count]]$mu0 <- c(0.2, dist.priors[[dclass]]$means[i])
    dist.forecastparams[[count]]$V0 <- diag(c(0.04, dist.priors[[dclass]]$vars[i]))
    dist.forecastparams[[count]]$name <- paste0(dist.name, i)
    count <- count + 1
  }
}
```

```{r}
## BIOMASS

Yw <- bextract*B2C*1000*1e-4 ## convert Mg/ha (Mg per hectacre)  to  kg C [356 (num ensemble members) x 28 (num years observed)]
Rw <- (84*B2C*1000*1e-4)^2 ## Observation Error: Kennedy et al 2018 Environ. Res. Lett. 13 025004; Fig 2 RMSE
## units: Mg/ha -> kg/m2
print(dim(Yw))
## grab the distribution of AGB for the first time point from all pixels
AGBprior <- Yw[,1]
ne = length(AGBprior) ## number of ensemble members

## spin up
PARlong <- as.vector(t(rad)) # concatenate PAR time series for each site into one vector
spin = VSEM(theta,PARlong) # Question: why run VSEM on the concatenated PAR? What is theta?
thin = seq(nrow(spin)/2,nrow(spin),length=ne)
spinIC = spin[thin,2:4] # select ne samples from the spin-up 
#for(i in 2:4){
#  hist(spin[thin,i],type='l')
#}

## disturbance recovery trajectory
nNBG = 200 ## years
NBG <- array(NA,c(ne,nNBG,3))
for(i in 1:ne){
  param = theta
  param[9:11] <- spinIC[i,]*c(0.01,1,0.01) ## set leaf and wood to 1% (simulate disturbance)
  raw = VSEM(param,PARlong[1:(nNBG*365.25)]) # simulate for nNBG years
  NBG[i,,] = raw[round(seq(365,nNBG*365.25,length=nNBG)),2:4]  ## grab pools at the end of each year
}
  
## for each AGBprior, grab the matching leaf and soil
ICprior <- matrix(NA,ne,3)
age = rep(NA,ne)
for(i in 1:ne){
  age[i] <- which.min((AGBprior[i]-NBG[i,,3])^2) # age = year in the disturbance recover trajectory where the simulated site has similar AGB to the AGB prior information
  ICprior[i,] <- c(NBG[i,age[i],1:2],AGBprior[i]) # use AGBprior for the model ICs
}
hist(age)
colnames(ICprior) <- c("Cv","Cs","CR") 
pairs(ICprior)
```

```{r}

## ---- Site-independent setup (computed once) --------------------------------
## Number of disturbance sub-classes and number of assimilation years.
n.dist = length(dist.forecastparams)
NT = floor(ncol(rad)/365)

## Background disturbance-type probability per forecast component, by matching
## the component's name to one of "other"/"cut"/"fire"/"biotic".
distname.toidx <- list("other"=2, "cut"=3, "fire"=4, "biotic"=5)
dist.prior.probs <- sapply(dist.forecastparams, function(x) {
  name <- x$name
  for (d in names(distname.toidx)) {
    if (grepl(d, name)) {
      return(d.prior[distname.toidx[[d]]])
    }
  }
})

## Diagonal process-error covariance (per-pool SDs) and prior process-precision
Q = diag(c(Ql,Qsoil,Qw)^2)

## Default heteroskedastic Rparams for GEDI (slope, intercept).
Rparams.GEDI.het <- c(0.01331, 0.09761)
Rparams.GEDI.fixed <- c(0.0000000, 0.8848249)
Rparams.Landtrendr.het <- c(0.013310, 3.012645)
Rparams.Landtrendr.fixed <- c(0.000, 3.79986)

## ---- Per-site argument builder ---------------------------------------------
## make_or_args(site, useDistProduct) assembles the site-specific inputs to
## ORJointUpdate: the (n.dist+1) x NT prior probability matrix p.dist (row 1 =
## undisturbed, rows 2.. = disturbance sub-classes), the bundled disturb.params,
## the NT x 3 observation matrix Y (wood-pool obs in column 3), and the PAR
## driver for that site. Relies on the site-independent globals above plus
## d.prior, dist.priors, dist.forecastparams, dextract, Yw and rad.
make_or_args <- function(site, useDistProduct = TRUE) {
  ## Initialize every year with the background prior (same column for all t).
  p.dist <- array(NA, dim = c(n.dist + 1, NT))
  for (t in 1:NT) {
    p.dist[1:(n.dist+1), t] <- as.numeric(c(d.prior[1], unlist(dist.prior.probs)))
  }

  ## If using the disturbance product, override the prior in years where a
  ## disturbance was detected at this site: replace that class's prior with the
  ## user's-accuracy estimate (Kennedy et al. 2015 table 6). Then give each
  ## component a share of the disturbance probability proportional to its weight,
  ## and the disturbed values to sum to 1 if they sum to greater than 1, and else
  ## set the undisturbed value to 1 - p(disturbed).
  ## within-class mixture weights (mclust proportions; sum to 1 within each class)
  weights <- unlist(sapply(dist.priors, function(x) x$weights))

  if (useDistProduct) {
    distidx.toname = list("10"="OTHER", "20"="CUT", "40"="FIRE", "50"="PEST")
    users_accuracy = c(1-d.prior[1], .77, .92, .77, .78, .78) ## 0 = none, 10 = other, 20 = cut, 30 = road, 40 = fire, 50 = biotic

    for (d in seq(names(dist.priors))) {
      d.name <- names(dist.priors)[d]
      has.dist <- which(dextract[site,] == d.name)
      if (length(has.dist) > 0) {
        is.dist <- which(names(dist.prior.probs) == distidx.toname[[d.name]]) + 1
        p.dist[is.dist, has.dist] <- users_accuracy[dextract[site, has.dist]/10 + 1]
      }
    }
  }

  ## Build the per-year categorical prior for BOTH the product and no-product paths:
  ## split each class's probability across its clusters via `weights` (so multi-cluster
  ## classes are not over-counted), then set the undisturbed prior to the remaining mass
  ## (= 1 - product accuracy in flagged years, = background otherwise). Applying this on
  ## the no-product path too means an UNflagged year has the same prior with or without
  ## the product -- the product only changes flagged years. Previously this lived inside
  ## the useDistProduct branch, so the no-product path kept an un-split, over-counted
  ## disturbance background that inflated probD relative to the product on unflagged sites.
  for (j in 1:ncol(p.dist)) {
    p.dist[2:(n.dist+1), j] <- p.dist[2:(n.dist+1), j] * weights   # split class prob across clusters
    dist.mass <- sum(p.dist[2:(n.dist+1), j])
    if (dist.mass > 1) {                                           # guard: cap total disturbed mass at 1
      p.dist[2:(n.dist+1), j] <- p.dist[2:(n.dist+1), j] / dist.mass
      dist.mass <- 1
    }
    p.dist[1, j] <- 1 - dist.mass                                  # undisturbed = remaining mass
  }

  ## Bundle the disturbance prior + per-class forecast params.
  disturb.params <- list(
    p = p.dist,
    n = n.dist,
    vals = dist.forecastparams,
    alloc.soil = 0.05
  )

  ## NT x 3 observation matrix with the wood-pool obs in column 3.
  Y <- matrix(NA, NT, 3)
  Y[1:ncol(Yw), 3] <- Yw[site, ]

  list(Y = Y, disturb.params = disturb.params, PAR = rad[site, ], site = site)
}
```


```{r}
# Helper functions for ORJointUpdate

KalmanUpdate <- function(m, C, H, R, y) {
  S <- H %*% C %*% t(H) + R
  K <- C %*% t(H) %*% solve(S)
  m_hat <- m + K %*% (y - H %*% m)
  C_hat <- (diag(nrow(C)) - K %*% H) %*% C
  L_hat <- dnorm(y, mean = H %*% m, sd = sqrt(S))
  
  return(list(m_hat=m_hat, C_hat=C_hat, L_hat=L_hat))
}

# gauss laguerre nodes / weights
# desired integral is \int_0^\infty f(\tau) \tau^{\alpha} e^{-\beta \tau} d\tau
# make the substitution x = \beta \cdot \tau
# integral with substitution is \int_0^\infty f(x / \beta) x^{\alpha} \beta^{-(\alpha+1)} e^{-x} dx
# this integral is now in the standard form, and gets approximated with weights 
# w_k \cdot \beta^{-(\alpha+1)} and nodes x_k / \beta
# where the weights w_k and nodes x_k come from gauss-laguerre quadrature
gauss_laguerre_rate <- function(n, alpha, beta) {
  gq <- gauss.quad(n, kind = "laguerre", alpha = alpha)  # weight x^alpha e^{-x}
  list(nodes   = gq$nodes / beta, # \tau = x / \beta
       weights = gq$weights / beta^(alpha + 1)) # transform weights to tau^alpha e^{-beta \cdot tau}
}

integrate_gl <- function(f, gq) sum(gq$weights * sapply(gq$nodes, f))

# solve the following equation for a and fixed c using newton's method:
# digamma(a) - log(a) = c
solve_digamma_log <- function(c, tol = 1e-12, maxiter = 100, a.max = 1e4) {
  if (!is.finite(c) || c >= 0) return(a.max)            # degenerate: cap shape
  s  <- -c
  a0 <- (3 - s + sqrt((s - 3)^2 + 24 * s)) / (12 * s)   # Minka initial guess
  g  <- function(a) digamma(a)  - log(a) - c
  gp <- function(a) trigamma(a) - 1 / a
  # newtonRaphson can *throw* (e.g. "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed") when an
  # iterate diverges to NaN; catch that so we fall back to a bracketed solve.
  a  <- tryCatch(
    suppressWarnings(newtonRaphson(fun = g, x0 = a0, dfun = gp,
                                   tol = tol, maxiter = maxiter)$root),
    error = function(e) NA_real_)
  if (!is.finite(a) || a <= 0 || abs(g(a)) > 1e-6)
    a <- tryCatch(uniroot(g, c(1e-8, a.max))$root, error = function(e) a.max)
  min(a, a.max)
}
```


```{r}
##' Approximate joint disturbance update (working-doc 6.30.26 algorithm).
##' Quadrature over the process precision tau: G Gauss-Laguerre nodes tau_g are chosen to
##' integrate against the Gamma(a,b) prior tau^{a-1} e^{-b tau}. Conditional on each tau_g
##' we run a Gaussian-sum filter with D components (undisturbed + dist$n disturbance
##' classes), each backed by an ensemble; the per-node log-evidence L_t(tau_g) is
##' accumulated and combined across nodes via log-sum-exp to weight the tau grid.
##'
##' @param gamInit c(a, b) Gamma prior (shape, rate) for tau
##' @param Y NT x 3 observations (wood/AGB pool in column 3; NA => forecast-only step)
##' @param Rparams c(slope, intercept): observation error R = y*slope + intercept
##' @param Q process-error covariance; Q[1,1],Q[2,2] used for foliage/soil, Q[3,3] set to 1/tau_g
##' @param PAR daily PAR driver (length NT*365)
##' @param Xic J x 3 initial-condition ensemble (ICprior); seeds every node's ensemble at t=1
##' @param THETA VSEM parameter vector/matrix (cols 9:11 overwritten with the IC ensemble)
##' @param dist disturbance list: p (D x NT prior), n (# classes), vals (per-class mu0/V0), alloc.soil
##' @param G number of Gauss-Laguerre precision nodes
ORJointUpdate <- function(gamInit, Y, Rparams, Q, PAR, Xic, THETA, dist, G = 200) {

  ## ---- dimensions ----
  NT <- length(PAR) / 365
  J  <- nrow(Xic)                       # ensemble size per (component, node); ICprior seeds it
  D  <- dist$n + 1                      # 1 undisturbed + dist$n disturbance sub-classes
  H  <- matrix(c(0, 0, 1), 1, 3)
  if (!is.matrix(THETA)) THETA <- matrix(THETA, nrow = J, ncol = length(THETA), byrow = TRUE)

  ## ---- Gauss-Laguerre nodes/weights for tau ~ Gamma(a,b): weight tau^{a-1} e^{-b tau} ----
  ## The weights already carry the Gamma kernel, so the tau-node posterior is
  ## W_g proportional to omega_g * L_t(tau_g) (no extra tau^{a-1} e^{-b tau} factor).
  a <- gamInit[1]; b <- gamInit[2]
  gl   <- gauss_laguerre_rate(G, a - 1, b)
  tau  <- gl$nodes
  logw <- log(gl$weights)
  logL <- rep(0, G)                     # log L_t(tau_g), accumulated evidence

  ## ---- moment-match a weighted set of 3-D Gaussians to one Gaussian ----
  mm <- function(ws, mus, Sigs) {
    W <- sum(ws)
    if (!is.finite(W) || W <= 0) return(NULL)
    wn <- ws / W
    mu <- rowSums(mapply(function(a, m) a * m, wn, mus))
    C  <- matrix(0, 3, 3)
    for (i in seq_along(wn)) C <- C + wn[i] * (Sigs[[i]] + tcrossprod(mus[[i]] - mu))
    list(w = W, mu = mu, Sigma = C)
  }

  ## VSEM parameter template: cols 1:8 are shared model params, 9:11 the state ICs that
  ## each sigma point overwrites. (THETA arrives as a matrix of identical rows.)
  th0 <- if (is.matrix(THETA)) THETA[1, ] else THETA

  ## ---- SIGMA-POINT (unscented) pushforward + disturbance split (PRECISION-INDEPENDENT) ----
  ## The forecast only needs the mean/cov of the pushforward per label, so we replace the
  ## J-member Monte-Carlo pushforward with the unscented transform: 2n+1 = 7 deterministic
  ## sigma points (n = 3 state dims) that match the input Gaussian N(m, P), pushed through
  ## VSEM ONCE and reused across ALL labels (undisturbed + each disturbance class). VSEM
  ## therefore runs 7 times per component instead of J. See claude-sigma-points-7.15.26.tex.
  ## Precision-independent: the wood-pool process error N(0, 1/tau_g) is added per node in
  ## the g-loop, so cSig[[1]] here is the tau-free pushforward spread.
  ut_pushforward <- function(m, P, tsel) {
    n <- 3; alpha <- 1e-3; beta.ut <- 2; kappa <- 0
    lam <- alpha^2 * (n + kappa) - n
    Ps  <- (P + t(P)) / 2 + diag(1e-9, 3)                 # symmetrize + jitter
    Lc  <- tryCatch(t(chol((n + lam) * Ps)),              # columns = sqrt((n+lam)P)
                    error = function(e) {
                      ev <- eigen((n + lam) * Ps, symmetric = TRUE)
                      ev$vectors %*% diag(sqrt(pmax(ev$values, 0))) %*% t(ev$vectors)
                    })
    X  <- cbind(m, m + Lc, m - Lc)                        # 3 x 7 sigma points
    wm <- c(lam / (n + lam), rep(1 / (2 * (n + lam)), 2 * n))
    wc <- wm; wc[1] <- wc[1] + (1 - alpha^2 + beta.ut)

    ## push the 7 points through VSEM ONCE (shared across every label)
    Y <- matrix(NA, 3, 2 * n + 1)
    for (i in 1:(2 * n + 1)) {
      th <- th0; th[9:11] <- pmax(X[, i], 1e-6)           # positivity guard on ICs
      Y[, i] <- VSEM(th, PAR = PAR[tsel])[365, 2:4]
    }
    Y <- pmax(Y, 1e-6)

    cmu <- vector("list", D); cSig <- vector("list", D)
    ## undisturbed: UT moment reconstruction WITHOUT process noise (Qg added per node)
    m1 <- as.numeric(Y %*% wm)
    P1 <- matrix(0, 3, 3)
    for (i in 1:(2 * n + 1)) { dd <- Y[, i] - m1; P1 <- P1 + wc[i] * tcrossprod(dd) }
    cmu[[1]] <- m1; cSig[[1]] <- P1

    ## disturbance classes: reuse the SAME propagated Y. The disturbance operator is affine
    ## in its Gaussian draw, so its conditional moments mu_d(y), Sig_d(y) are closed-form;
    ## the class forecast moments follow by the law of total variance (between-point spread
    ## of mu_d + weighted-mean within-point noise Sig_d). No sampling of disturbance.p.
    for (d in 1:dist$n) {
      mu0 <- dist$vals[[d]]$mu0; V0 <- dist$vals[[d]]$V0; s <- dist$alloc.soil
      MU <- matrix(NA, 3, 2 * n + 1); within <- matrix(0, 3, 3)
      for (i in 1:(2 * n + 1)) {
        yi <- Y[, i]
        MU[, i] <- c(mu0[1] * yi[1],                                        # eq (mu_d): retain
                     yi[2] + s * ((1 - mu0[1]) * yi[1] + (1 - mu0[2]) * yi[3]),  # residual -> soil
                     mu0[2] * yi[3])
        d1 <- yi[1]^2 * V0[1, 1]; d2 <- yi[3]^2 * V0[2, 2]                  # eq (Sig_d) = A D0 A^T
        Sd <- matrix(c( d1,       -s * d1,           0,
                       -s * d1,    s^2 * (d1 + d2),  -s * d2,
                        0,         -s * d2,           d2), 3, 3, byrow = TRUE)
        within <- within + wm[i] * Sd
      }
      md <- as.numeric(MU %*% wm)
      between <- matrix(0, 3, 3)
      for (i in 1:(2 * n + 1)) { e <- MU[, i] - md; between <- between + wc[i] * tcrossprod(e) }
      cmu[[d + 1]] <- md; cSig[[d + 1]] <- between + within
    }
    list(mu = cmu, Sig = cSig)
  }

  ## ---- state carried across time (PRECISION-MARGINAL): D Gaussian components (label k) ----
  ## Rao-Blackwellization: rather than G copies of the state (one per tau node), carry a
  ## single tau-marginal mixture of D components. With the sigma-point forecast there is no
  ## ensemble: each component is carried as its Gaussian moments (bar.mu, bar.Sig), from
  ## which the 7 sigma points are regenerated each step. Each step re-expands over the G
  ## nodes by adding the node-specific process error Qg analytically; the tau posterior W_g
  ## is tracked separately (logL). Xic seeds the t=1 component's mean and covariance.
  bar.w   <- numeric(D)                  # tau-marginal component (label) weights, sum = 1
  bar.mu  <- matrix(0, D, 3)             # component means (input Gaussian for the pushforward)
  bar.Sig <- array(0, dim = c(D, 3, 3))  # component covariances
  bar.w[1]    <- 1                       # t=1: single undisturbed component
  bar.mu[1, ] <- colMeans(as.matrix(Xic))
  bar.Sig[1, , ] <- var(as.matrix(Xic))

  ## diagnostics (same fields as before so downstream analysis keeps working)
  hist <- list(y=rep(NA,NT), overall.analysis=rep(NA,NT),
               analysis.dist=rep(NA,NT), analysis.undist=rep(NA,NT),
               forecast.dist=rep(NA,NT), forecast.undist=rep(NA,NT),
               ci.mean=rep(NA,NT), ci.lower=rep(NA,NT), ci.upper=rep(NA,NT),
               probD=rep(NA,NT), ci5=matrix(NA,NT,5), nis=rep(NA,NT),
               nis.cf=rep(NA,NT), nis.q33=rep(NA,NT), nis.R=rep(NA,NT), nis.innov=rep(NA,NT))

  for (t in 1:NT) {
    print(paste0("timestep: ", t))
    y    <- Y[t, 3]
    tsel <- (t - 1) * 365 + 1:365
    Kin  <- if (t == 1) 1 else D          # # input components per node
    ## component weights beta_k = 1{k=1}(1-p_t) + 1{k>=2} p_t * pi_k, with p_t the total
    ## disturbance probability (from dist$p) and pi_k the uniform disturbance-forecast
    ## mixing 1/dist$n (matching the ensemble split c(0.5, rep(0.5/dist$n, dist$n))).
    p_t  <- 1 - dist$p[1, t]                           # total disturbance probability
    beta <- c(dist$p[1, t], rep(p_t / dist$n, dist$n)) # undist + uniform type-mixing (length D)
    R    <- if (is.na(y)) NA_real_ else y * Rparams[1] + Rparams[2]

    ## ---- precision-INDEPENDENT sigma-point pushforward: 7 VSEM runs per input component c ----
    ## Rao-Blackwellization: the G precision nodes reuse these shared moments (adding only
    ## their node-specific Qg), so VSEM runs 7*Kin times per step instead of 7*Kin*G.
    push <- vector("list", Kin)
    for (c in 1:Kin) if (bar.w[c] > 0) push[[c]] <- ut_pushforward(bar.mu[c, ], bar.Sig[c, , ], tsel)

    fc.w    <- matrix(0, D, G)            # forecast mixture (for NIS) per (k,g)
    fc.mu   <- array(NA, dim = c(D, 3, G))
    fc.Sig  <- array(NA, dim = c(D, 3, 3, G))
    logZ    <- rep(0, G)

    ## raw (uncollapsed) Kalman-updated components, kept for the final Pi_D so it
    ## aggregates all G*K*D components directly (not the per-node Pi_K collapse).
    ## Per label k: within-node weights alpha^{c,k,g}=up.w/Z_g, means, covs, and node id g.
    allk.alpha <- vector("list", D); allk.mu <- vector("list", D)
    allk.Sig   <- vector("list", D); allk.node <- vector("list", D)
    ## and the raw forecast (pre-Kalman) components, kept as the full D*K*G mixture so NIS
    ## can collapse just the dominant label's components (not the per-node Pi_K collapse).
    allf.w <- vector("list", D); allf.mu <- vector("list", D)
    allf.Sig <- vector("list", D); allf.node <- vector("list", D); allf.q33 <- vector("list", D)
    for (k in 1:D) { allk.alpha[[k]] <- numeric(); allk.mu[[k]] <- list()
                     allk.Sig[[k]] <- list(); allk.node[[k]] <- integer()
                     allf.w[[k]] <- numeric(); allf.mu[[k]] <- list()
                     allf.Sig[[k]] <- list(); allf.node[[k]] <- integer(); allf.q33[[k]] <- numeric() }

    for (g in 1:G) {
      ## node-specific process error on the wood pool: Qg[3,3] = 1/tau_g (added analytically
      ## to the shared, precision-independent pushforward covariance for the undisturbed label)
      Qg <- Q; Qg[3, 3] <- 1 / tau[g]
      if (!is.finite(Qg[3, 3]) || Qg[3, 3] <= 0) Qg[3, 3] <- 1e-6

      ## per-label accumulators over input components c
      up.w   <- vector("list", D); up.mu <- vector("list", D); up.Sig <- vector("list", D)
      fc.acc.w <- vector("list", D); fc.acc.mu <- vector("list", D); fc.acc.Sig <- vector("list", D)
      fc.acc.q33 <- vector("list", D)
      for (k in 1:D) { up.w[[k]] <- numeric(); up.mu[[k]] <- list(); up.Sig[[k]] <- list()
                       fc.acc.w[[k]] <- numeric(); fc.acc.mu[[k]] <- list(); fc.acc.Sig[[k]] <- list()
                       fc.acc.q33[[k]] <- numeric() }

      for (c in 1:Kin) {
        if (bar.w[c] <= 0) next
        fs <- push[[c]]                                      # shared VSEM pushforward (no tau)
        for (k in 1:D) {
          ## fold in the node-specific process error on the undisturbed label only; the
          ## disturbance labels carry no process error (q33 = 0). fs$Sig[[1]] is the tau-free
          ## ensemble spread, so Sig.fk = ensemble + Qg is the OVERALL forecast covariance.
          Sig.fk <- fs$Sig[[k]]; q33.fk <- 0
          if (k == 1) { Sig.fk <- Sig.fk + Qg; q33.fk <- Qg[3, 3] }
          mu.fk  <- fs$mu[[k]]
          w.fk <- bar.w[c] * beta[k]                         # forecast-mixture weight
          ## forecast mixture (label k) accumulation for NIS
          fc.acc.w[[k]]   <- c(fc.acc.w[[k]], w.fk)
          fc.acc.mu[[k]]  <- c(fc.acc.mu[[k]], list(mu.fk))
          fc.acc.Sig[[k]] <- c(fc.acc.Sig[[k]], list(Sig.fk))
          fc.acc.q33[[k]] <- c(fc.acc.q33[[k]], q33.fk)      # process-error part of Sigma[3,3]
          if (!is.na(y)) {                                   # observed: Kalman update
            ku <- KalmanUpdate(mu.fk, Sig.fk, H, R, y)
            up.w[[k]]   <- c(up.w[[k]], w.fk * as.numeric(ku$L_hat))
            up.mu[[k]]  <- c(up.mu[[k]], list(as.numeric(ku$m_hat)))
            up.Sig[[k]] <- c(up.Sig[[k]], list(ku$C_hat))
          } else {                                           # no obs: carry forecast (lik = 1)
            up.w[[k]]   <- c(up.w[[k]], w.fk)
            up.mu[[k]]  <- c(up.mu[[k]], list(mu.fk))
            up.Sig[[k]] <- c(up.Sig[[k]], list(Sig.fk))
          }
        }
      }

      ## Z_t(tau_g) = sum over all (c,k) updated weights; alpha normalizes within node
      Zg <- sum(unlist(up.w))
      logZ[g] <- if (is.na(y)) 0 else if (Zg > 0) log(Zg) else -Inf
      norm <- if (Zg > 0) Zg else 1

      for (k in 1:D) {
        ## stash the raw (c) components of this (k,g) for the final Pi_D (all G*K*D)
        if (length(up.w[[k]]) > 0) {
          allk.alpha[[k]] <- c(allk.alpha[[k]], up.w[[k]] / norm)   # alpha^{c,k,g} = up.w / Z_g
          allk.mu[[k]]    <- c(allk.mu[[k]], up.mu[[k]])
          allk.Sig[[k]]   <- c(allk.Sig[[k]], up.Sig[[k]])
          allk.node[[k]]  <- c(allk.node[[k]], rep(g, length(up.w[[k]])))
        }
        ## stash the raw (c) FORECAST components of this (k,g) for the full-mixture NIS.
        ## Weight per component = bar.w[c,g]*beta_k (in fc.acc.w); node index kept for W_g.
        if (length(fc.acc.w[[k]]) > 0) {
          allf.w[[k]]    <- c(allf.w[[k]], fc.acc.w[[k]])
          allf.mu[[k]]   <- c(allf.mu[[k]], fc.acc.mu[[k]])
          allf.Sig[[k]]  <- c(allf.Sig[[k]], fc.acc.Sig[[k]])
          allf.node[[k]] <- c(allf.node[[k]], rep(g, length(fc.acc.w[[k]])))
          allf.q33[[k]]  <- c(allf.q33[[k]], fc.acc.q33[[k]])
        }
        ## forecast mixture collapse (for NIS diagnostics)
        if (length(fc.acc.w[[k]]) > 0 && sum(fc.acc.w[[k]]) > 0) {
          fcoll <- mm(fc.acc.w[[k]], fc.acc.mu[[k]], fc.acc.Sig[[k]])
          fc.w[k, g]      <- fcoll$w
          fc.mu[k, , g]   <- fcoll$mu
          fc.Sig[k, , , g] <- fcoll$Sigma
        }
      }
      ## NOTE: no per-node Pi_K collapse or per-node resample here. Under
      ## Rao-Blackwellization the carried state is the single tau-marginal Pi_D mixture
      ## (computed after the g-loop); one ensemble per label is resampled from it below.
    } # end g

    ## accumulate evidence and compute the tau-node posterior W_g via log-sum-exp
    logL <- logL + logZ
    logm <- logw + logL
    mmax <- max(logm[is.finite(logm)])
    W <- exp(logm - mmax); W[!is.finite(W)] <- 0; W <- W / sum(W)

    ## final Pi_D: aggregate ALL raw G*K*D Kalman-updated components by label k, each
    ## weighted by W_g * alpha^{c,k,g}. Uses the uncollapsed components (allk.*) so the
    ## between-c spread within each (k,g) is retained in Sig.k (not lost to the Pi_K step).
    eta <- rep(0, D); mu.k <- matrix(0, D, 3); Sig.k <- array(0, dim = c(D, 3, 3))
    for (k in 1:D) {
      if (length(allk.alpha[[k]]) == 0) next
      ws  <- W[allk.node[[k]]] * allk.alpha[[k]]             # W_g * alpha^{c,k,g}
      sel <- which(ws > 0)
      if (length(sel) == 0) next
      coll <- mm(ws[sel], allk.mu[[k]][sel], allk.Sig[[k]][sel])
      eta[k] <- coll$w; mu.k[k, ] <- coll$mu; Sig.k[k, , ] <- coll$Sigma
    }
    eta <- eta / sum(eta)

    ## ---- carry the tau-MARGINAL Pi_D mixture forward as the next step's D components ----
    ## Rao-Blackwellization: the carried state is a single node-independent D-component
    ## Gaussian mixture (not G copies). With the sigma-point forecast the moments ARE the
    ## state -- no ensemble to resample; the 7 sigma points are regenerated from (bar.mu,
    ## bar.Sig) next step. Without this the mixture would collapse to the t=1 component.
    bar.w   <- eta
    bar.mu  <- mu.k
    bar.Sig <- Sig.k

    ## ---- diagnostics (wood/AGB pool = index 3) ----
    di <- 2:D; swd <- sum(eta[di]); gs <- which.max(eta)
    hist$y[t]                <- y
    hist$overall.analysis[t] <- sum(eta * mu.k[, 3])
    hist$analysis.undist[t]  <- if (eta[1] > 0) mu.k[1, 3] else NA
    hist$analysis.dist[t]    <- if (swd > 0) sum(eta[di] * mu.k[di, 3]) / swd else NA
    hist$probD[t]            <- swd
    cm <- mu.k[gs, 3]; vv <- max(Sig.k[gs, 3, 3], 0)
    hist$ci.mean[t]  <- cm
    hist$ci.lower[t] <- cm - 1.96 * sqrt(vv)
    hist$ci.upper[t] <- cm + 1.96 * sqrt(vv)
    hist$ci5[t, ]    <- normal_quantile(c(.025, .25, .5, .75, .975), cm, vv)

    ## forecast-mixture means (node-posterior weighted) for reporting
    fmean <- sapply(1:D, function(k) {
      ws <- W * fc.w[k, ]; s <- which(ws > 0)
      if (length(s) == 0) return(NA); sum(ws[s] * fc.mu[k, 3, s]) / sum(ws[s])
    })
    fw.k <- sapply(1:D, function(k) sum(W * fc.w[k, ]))
    hist$forecast.undist[t] <- fmean[1]
    hist$forecast.dist[t]   <- if (sum(fw.k[di]) > 0) sum(fw.k[di] * fmean[di], na.rm = TRUE) / sum(fw.k[di]) else NA

    ## NIS against the dominant label gs: collapse ITS full set of raw forecast components
    ## (all c and g, i.e. the label-gs slice of the D*K*G forecast mixture -- not the
    ## per-node Pi_K collapse), so the between-c spread is retained in S. Each component is
    ## weighted by W_g * (bar.w[c,g] * beta_gs), where allf.w already holds bar.w*beta_gs.
    if (!is.na(y)) {
      ws <- W[allf.node[[gs]]] * allf.w[[gs]]; s <- which(ws > 0)
      if (length(s) > 0) {
        fck <- mm(ws[s], allf.mu[[gs]][s], allf.Sig[[gs]][s])
        S <- fck$Sigma[3, 3] + R
        ## Decompose the collapsed forecast variance S - R = fck$Sigma[3,3] into the
        ## process-error part (weighted mean of the components' q33 = Qg[3,3]) and the rest
        ## (ensemble + between-component spread). Since Sigma[3,3] = ensemble + q33 for each
        ## component, the weighted-mean q33 is the process share of the collapsed variance.
        q33.bar <- sum(ws[s] * allf.q33[[gs]][s]) / sum(ws[s])
        hist$nis[t]     <- if (is.finite(S) && S > 0) (y - fck$mu[3])^2 / S else NA
        hist$nis.q33[t] <- q33.bar                                  # process-error part
        hist$nis.cf[t]  <- fck$Sigma[3, 3] - q33.bar                # ensemble + between-comp spread
        hist$nis.R[t]   <- R
        hist$nis.innov[t] <- y - fck$mu[3]
      }
    }
  } # end t

  return(hist)
}

```

```{r}
## Generate ORJointUpdate inputs for each requested site, run the joint update,
## and save each site's diagnostics to experiments/jointUpdate. Returns the
## results invisibly (keyed by site) for convenience.
## Rparams.source ("GEDI"/"LandTrendr") and Rparams.model ("het"/"con") describe the
## observation-error parameters in use; they are recorded in each output filename.
run_joint_update_sites <- function(site.idx, Rparams = Rparams.GEDI.het,
                                   useDistProduct = TRUE,
                                   Rparams.source = c("GEDI", "LandTrendr"),
                                   Rparams.model  = c("het", "con"),
                                   outdir = "experiments/jointUpdateNewTest") {
  Rparams.source <- match.arg(Rparams.source)
  Rparams.model  <- match.arg(Rparams.model)
  if (!dir.exists(outdir)) dir.create(outdir, recursive = TRUE)
  results <- list()
  for (site in site.idx) {
    message("running joint update for site ", site)
    args <- make_or_args(site, useDistProduct)
    out <- ORJointUpdate(gamInit = gamInit, Y = args$Y, Rparams = Rparams,
                         Q = Q, PAR = args$PAR, Xic = ICprior,
                         THETA = theta[1:11], dist = args$disturb.params)
    fname <- file.path(outdir,
                       sprintf("site_%d_distprod_%s_%s_%s.rds",
                               site, useDistProduct, Rparams.source, Rparams.model))
    saveRDS(out, fname)
    results[[as.character(site)]] <- out
  }
  invisible(results)
}
```

```{r}
# Plot wood/AGB pool trajectories: observation, analysis & forecast means
# (overall / disturbed / undisturbed), and the 95% CI of the most likely component.
res <- readRDS("experiments/jointUpdate/site_391_distprod_TRUE_GEDI_het.rds")
tt <- seq_along(res$y)
ylim <- range(c(res$y, res$ci.lower, res$ci.upper, res$overall.analysis,
                res$analysis.dist, res$analysis.undist,
                res$forecast.dist, res$forecast.undist), na.rm=TRUE)
plot(tt, res$overall.analysis, type="n", ylim=ylim,
     xlab="timestep (year)", ylab="wood / AGB pool (kg C m-2)",
     main="OR joint update - wood pool")
ok <- is.finite(res$ci.lower) & is.finite(res$ci.upper)
polygon(c(tt[ok], rev(tt[ok])), c(res$ci.lower[ok], rev(res$ci.upper[ok])),
        col=adjustcolor("grey70", 0.4), border=NA)
lines(tt, res$overall.analysis, col="black",       lwd=2)
lines(tt, res$analysis.undist,  col="forestgreen", lwd=2)
#lines(tt, res$analysis.dist,    col="firebrick",   lwd=2)
lines(tt, res$forecast.undist,  col="forestgreen", lwd=1, lty=2)
lines(tt, res$forecast.dist,    col="firebrick",   lwd=1, lty=2)
points(tt, res$y, pch=19, col="blue")
legend("topleft", bty="n", cex=0.8,
  legend=c("Y (obs)","overall analysis","analysis undist","analysis dist",
           "forecast undist","forecast dist","95% CI (top comp)"),
  col=c("blue","black","forestgreen","firebrick","forestgreen","firebrick","grey70"),
  pch=c(19,NA,NA,NA,NA,NA,15), lty=c(NA,1,1,1,2,2,NA), lwd=c(NA,2,2,2,1,1,NA))
```

```{r}
## Test the new method on one sample site: overlay the analysis mean + 95% CI band
## (dominant posterior component) with the yearly wood/AGB observation.
testdir  <- "experiments/jointUpdateNewTest"
testsite <- 300
res <- readRDS(file.path(testdir, sprintf("site_%d_distprod_FALSE_GEDI_het.rds", testsite)))

yr <- dtime[1] + seq_along(res$y) - 1                 # calendar year per timestep (obs end < NT)
ok <- is.finite(res$ci.lower) & is.finite(res$ci.upper)
## restrict the shared year axis to years that actually have an observation, so the
## forecast-only tail doesn't stretch the axis and the CI band stays legible.
obs  <- is.finite(res$y)
xlim <- range(yr[obs])
win  <- yr >= xlim[1] & yr <= xlim[2]                 # timesteps inside the observed window
ylim <- range(c(res$y[win], res$ci.lower[win], res$ci.upper[win],
                res$overall.analysis[win]), na.rm = TRUE)

## two stacked panels sharing the year axis: state on top, P(disturbance) below
op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(0, 4.5, 3, 1), oma = c(4, 0, 0, 0))

## top: analysis mean + 95% CI band + observation
plot(yr, res$overall.analysis, type = "n", xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim, xaxt = "n", xlab = "",
     ylab = "wood / AGB pool (kg C m-2)",
     main = sprintf("New joint update - site %d", testsite))
polygon(c(yr[ok], rev(yr[ok])), c(res$ci.lower[ok], rev(res$ci.upper[ok])),
        col = adjustcolor("grey70", 0.4), border = NA)          # 95% CI band
lines(yr, res$overall.analysis, col = "black", lwd = 2)         # analysis mean
points(yr, res$y, pch = 19, col = "blue")                       # yearly observation
legend("topright", bty = "n", cex = 0.85,
       legend = c("observation", "analysis mean", "95% CI (dominant comp)"),
       col = c("blue", "black", "grey70"),
       pch = c(19, NA, 15), lty = c(NA, 1, NA), lwd = c(NA, 2, NA))

## bottom: posterior probability of disturbance (hist$probD)
par(mar = c(0, 4.5, 0, 1))
plot(yr, res$probD, type = "h", lwd = 3, col = "firebrick", xlim = xlim, ylim = c(0, 1),
     xlab = "", ylab = "P(disturbance)")
points(yr, res$probD, pch = 19, cex = 0.6, col = "firebrick")
mtext("year", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 2.5)
par(op)
```
